waleffe_abstract.source: F. Waleffe, On some dyadic models of the Euler equations, arXiv:math/0410380v2 (2004)
waleffe_abstract.text: Katz and Pavlovic recently proposed a dyadic model of the Euler equations for which they proved finite time blow-up in the H^{3/2+eps} Sobolev norm. It is shown that their model can be reduced to the dyadic inviscid Burgers equation where nonlinear interactions are restricted to dyadic wavenumbers. [...] Finite time blow-up in the H^alpha norm, with alpha > 0, is proven for a class of models that includes all those models.

waleffe_eq19_20.location: Section 5, equations (19)-(20) and the sentence after (20)
waleffe_eq19_20.text: Here, we consider the class of chain models da_j/dt = lambda^j a_{j-1}^2 - lambda^{j+1} a_j a_{j+1}, j > j_0 ; da_{j_0}/dt = -lambda^{j_0+1} a_{j_0} a_{j_0+1}, (19) for some integer j_0, where lambda > 1 and the a_j's are real. This includes the dyadic Burgers model (12) when lambda = 2 [...]. The total energy of system (19) is defined as E = sum_{j >= j_0} E_j < infinity, E_j = a_j^2. (20) It is easily verified that the total energy is preserved by the dynamics (19), thus E(t) = E(0), for all t > 0.

waleffe_thm1.text: Theorem 1. If a_j(t) is a solution to system (19) with a_j(0) >= 0, for all j and (32) E_{B(J)}(0) >= q^J for some sufficiently large integer J >= j_0 and lambda^{-2} < q < 1, then the H^alpha norm of the solution becomes unbounded in finite-time, for any alpha > 0.
